claims.text: Al0.1CrCoFeNi is a low-Al high-entropy alloy suitable for investigating temperature-dependent plastic deformation.
Before deformation, Al0.1CrCoFeNi is predominantly disordered FCC with weak chemical clustering.
Systematic temperature variation will drive Al0.1CrCoFeNi from a clustered, disordered state toward a more ordered state.
The clustering-to-ordering transition moderates dislocation dynamics and plastic deformation.
The proposed tests span cryogenic conditions through elevated temperatures up to approximately 900 °C under quasi-static, controlled loading.
Temperature changes the arrangement and mobility of dislocations in Al0.1CrCoFeNi.
Increasing temperature activates atomic rearrangement in Al0.1CrCoFeNi.
Increasing temperature reduces clustering and facilitates reordering in Al0.1CrCoFeNi.
Pronounced clustering at lower temperatures hinders deformation.
A more ordered microstructure at higher temperatures facilitates dislocation motion.
At lower temperatures, Al0.1CrCoFeNi will exhibit relatively high yield strength.
At lower temperatures, Al0.1CrCoFeNi will exhibit limited plasticity because of pronounced clustering.
At higher temperatures, Al0.1CrCoFeNi will exhibit lower yield strength.
At higher temperatures, Al0.1CrCoFeNi will exhibit increased ductility.
At ambient temperature, the Al0.1CrCoFeNi microstructure remains largely disordered and clustering is dominant.
The proposed behavior is primarily expected in low-Al CrCoFeNi high-entropy alloys.
The proposed behavior may not extend to substantially different HEA compositions or to single-element systems.
Possible contributions from twinning and other phase transformations remain unresolved.

contradictions.description: The initial state is described as having weak clustering, whereas the ambient-temperature baseline says clustering is dominant, without specifying a treatment or deformation history that would reconcile the difference.
